market_summary: Markets staged a sharp relief rally Monday (S&P +2.4%, Nasdaq100 +3.4%) as falling oil prices eased inflation fears after last week's selloff, with Tuesday's open hinging on the October CPI print. Nvidia is the standout loser, down ~4.3% and -22% over the month after CEO Jensen Huang's scandal/espionage-linked investigation disclosure, a governance overhang that lands right before its Nov 17 earnings. Singapore banks (DBS/OCBC/UOB, ~44% of STI) are rebounding off oversold levels (all 3 up 1-3% today) even as they turn more selective on AI-related lending, while SIA is investing S$2bn in cabin upgrades ahead of its Nov 11 results. Big-cap US tech (AAPL, MSFT) is riding the broad risk-on bounce, though valuations for AAPL look full versus consensus targets.

picks.thesis: Nvidia is in a confirmed downtrend (-22% 1m, -18.4% vs 50dMA) and now carries a fresh governance/reputational overhang from the CEO scandal, with an unresolved board investigation. Rel. volume is nearly 4x normal, showing heavy distribution. Earnings on Nov 17 add a binary risk catalyst while sentiment is impaired, making further downside or at least continued volatility likely before any fundamental re-rating.
picks.news: Board investigation launched into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted an affair with an alleged Chinese spy (2026-11-08); stock lost ~$200B in market value Monday on the disclosure (2026-11-08/09).
picks.risks: Chip fundamentals/demand remain extremely strong; if the investigation clears Huang quickly or earnings on Nov 17 beat materially, shares could snap back hard given how beaten down they already are and the extreme analyst upside (83% to consensus target).

picks.thesis: Microsoft is leading the tech rally (+2.75% Monday) and is actively lobbying against a proposed Chinese-transceiver ban that would hit AI data-center buildouts, signaling it is protecting its capex-heavy AI infrastructure plans. Price is solidly above both 50- and 200-day averages (+5.4%/+23.8%) and analyst consensus still implies ~17% upside with near-unanimous buy ratings (53 of 58).
picks.news: Microsoft pushing Trump administration to halt FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers used in AI data centers (2026-11-10); shares +2.75% in Monday's broad tech rally (2026-11-10).
picks.risks: If the transceiver ban proceeds and raises data-center costs, or if the broader risk-on rally fades once CPI data disappoints, MSFT could give back recent gains given its already-elevated valuation versus 1-month return.

picks.thesis: OCBC jumped 3.1% today and has the strongest 1-year return (+57%) of the three local banks while still trading 11% below its 52-week high, suggesting room to continue closing that gap as banks rebound from last month's pullback. It's trading comfortably above its 200-day average (+10.8%) despite a soft month, indicating the longer trend remains intact.
picks.news: Singapore banks (OCBC, UOB, DBS) staying selective but still actively courting AI/data-center financing deals amid strong regional demand (2026-11-09); OCBC +3.1% today in the broad market bounce (2026-11-10).
picks.risks: If credit concerns around debt-funded AI infrastructure spending escalate, or if the rebound is just a one-day beta bounce tied to the general market relief rally rather than bank-specific strength, gains could reverse quickly.

picks.thesis: UOB is the clear laggard among the three Singapore banks: worst 3-month return (-10.9%), below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, and the most balanced analyst view (only 4 buys vs 10 holds). Today's 1.4% bounce lagged peers' 3.1% and 0.9% gains, suggesting relative weakness persists even in a risk-on tape.
picks.news: Singapore banks turning selective on AI-related financing amid debt-risk concerns (2026-11-09), a sector-wide theme that may weigh more on UOB given its softer recent momentum and higher relative volume (1.59x) signalling distribution.
picks.risks: Banks often move together on rate/macro themes; if UOB's Q3 results (referenced in sector commentary) beat expectations or NIM trends improve, this laggard could quickly catch up to peers, especially as its analyst consensus still implies 10.4% upside.

picks.thesis: Keppel rallied 3.3% today and screens as deeply oversold, trading 25.9% below its 52-week high with a very bullish analyst base (12 buy, 2 hold, 1 sell) and consensus target implying 30% upside. This looks like a potential mean-reversion/value setup after a rough 3-6 months, though there's no fresh company-specific catalyst in the news flow to confirm a turn.</br>
picks.news: No stock-specific news item was found for Keppel in this cycle; today's +3.3% move appears tied to the broad market risk-on rally rather than a company catalyst (2026-11-10).
picks.risks: Lack of a specific catalyst means this is a lower-conviction, momentum/valuation-only call; continued weakness in its underlying business (reflected in -13.6% 3m return and elevated volatility of 25%) could mean the stock keeps underperforming rather than reverting.
